[627](https://docs.rs#627)
[628](https://docs.rs#628)/// A slice of a UTF-8 path (akin to [`str`]).
[629](https://docs.rs#629)///
[630](https://docs.rs#630)/// This type supports a number of operations for inspecting a path, including
[631](https://docs.rs#631)/// breaking the path into its components (separated by `/` on Unix and by either
[632](https://docs.rs#632)/// `/` or `\` on Windows), extracting the file name, determining whether the path
[633](https://docs.rs#633)/// is absolute, and so on.
[634](https://docs.rs#634)///
[635](https://docs.rs#635)/// This is an *unsized* type, meaning that it must always be used behind a
[636](https://docs.rs#636)/// pointer like `&` or [`Box`]. For an owned version of this type,
[637](https://docs.rs#637)/// see [`Utf8PathBuf`].
[638](https://docs.rs#638)///
[639](https://docs.rs#639)/// # Examples
[640](https://docs.rs#640)///
[641](https://docs.rs#641)/// ```
[642](https://docs.rs#642)/// use camino::Utf8Path;
[643](https://docs.rs#643)///
[644](https://docs.rs#644)/// // Note: this example does work on Windows
[645](https://docs.rs#645)/// let path = Utf8Path::new("./foo/bar.txt");
[646](https://docs.rs#646)///
[647](https://docs.rs#647)/// let parent = path.parent();
[648](https://docs.rs#648)/// assert_eq!(parent, Some(Utf8Path::new("./foo")));
[649](https://docs.rs#649)///
[650](https://docs.rs#650)/// let file_stem = path.file_stem();
[651](https://docs.rs#651)/// assert_eq!(file_stem, Some("bar"));
[652](https://docs.rs#652)///
[653](https://docs.rs#653)/// let extension = path.extension();
[654](https://docs.rs#654)/// assert_eq!(extension, Some("txt"));
[655](https://docs.rs#655)/// ```
[656](https://docs.rs#656)// NB: Internal Path must only contain utf8 data
[657](https://docs.rs#657)#[repr(transparent)]
[658](https://docs.rs#658)pub struct Utf8Path(Path);
[659](https://docs.rs#659)
[660](https://docs.rs#660)impl Utf8Path {
[661](https://docs.rs#661)    /// Directly wraps a string slice as a [`Utf8Path`] slice.
[662](https://docs.rs#662)    ///
[663](https://docs.rs#663)    /// This is a cost-free conversion.
[664](https://docs.rs#664)    ///
[665](https://docs.rs#665)    /// # Examples
[666](https://docs.rs#666)    ///
[667](https://docs.rs#667)    /// ```
[668](https://docs.rs#668)    /// use camino::Utf8Path;
[669](https://docs.rs#669)    ///
[670](https://docs.rs#670)    /// Utf8Path::new("foo.txt");
[671](https://docs.rs#671)    /// ```
[672](https://docs.rs#672)    ///
[673](https://docs.rs#673)    /// You can create [`Utf8Path`]s from [`String`]s, or even other [`Utf8Path`]s:
[674](https://docs.rs#674)    ///
[675](https://docs.rs#675)    /// ```
[676](https://docs.rs#676)    /// use camino::Utf8Path;
[677](https://docs.rs#677)    ///
[678](https://docs.rs#678)    /// let string = String::from("foo.txt");
[679](https://docs.rs#679)    /// let from_string = Utf8Path::new(&string);
[680](https://docs.rs#680)    /// let from_path = Utf8Path::new(&from_string);
[681](https://docs.rs#681)    /// assert_eq!(from_string, from_path);
[682](https://docs.rs#682)    /// ```
[683](https://docs.rs#683)    pub fn new(s: &(impl AsRef<str> + ?Sized)) -> &Utf8Path {
[684](https://docs.rs#684)        let path = Path::new(s.as_ref());
[685](https://docs.rs#685)        // SAFETY: s is a str which means it is always valid UTF-8
[686](https://docs.rs#686)        unsafe { Utf8Path::assume_utf8(path) }
[687](https://docs.rs#687)    }
[688](https://docs.rs#688)
[689](https://docs.rs#689)    /// Converts a [`Path`] to a [`Utf8Path`].
[690](https://docs.rs#690)    ///
[691](https://docs.rs#691)    /// Returns [`None`] if the path is not valid UTF-8.
[692](https://docs.rs#692)    ///
[693](https://docs.rs#693)    /// For a version that returns a type that implements [`std::error::Error`],
[694](https://docs.rs#694)    /// see [`TryFrom<&Path>`][tryfrom].
[695](https://docs.rs#695)    ///
[696](https://docs.rs#696)    /// [tryfrom]: #impl-TryFrom<%26Path>-for-%26Utf8Path
[697](https://docs.rs#697)    ///
[698](https://docs.rs#698)    /// # Examples
[699](https://docs.rs#699)    ///
[700](https://docs.rs#700)    /// ```
[701](https://docs.rs#701)    /// use camino::Utf8Path;
[702](https://docs.rs#702)    /// use std::ffi::OsStr;
[703](https://docs.rs#703)    /// # #[cfg(unix)]
[704](https://docs.rs#704)    /// use std::os::unix::ffi::OsStrExt;
[705](https://docs.rs#705)    /// use std::path::Path;
[706](https://docs.rs#706)    ///
[707](https://docs.rs#707)    /// let unicode_path = Path::new("/valid/unicode");
[708](https://docs.rs#708)    /// Utf8Path::from_path(unicode_path).expect("valid Unicode path succeeded");
[709](https://docs.rs#709)    ///
[710](https://docs.rs#710)    /// // Paths on Unix can be non-UTF-8.
[711](https://docs.rs#711)    /// # #[cfg(unix)]
[712](https://docs.rs#712)    /// let non_unicode_str = OsStr::from_bytes(b"\xFF\xFF\xFF");
[713](https://docs.rs#713)    /// # #[cfg(unix)]
[714](https://docs.rs#714)    /// let non_unicode_path = Path::new(non_unicode_str);
[715](https://docs.rs#715)    /// # #[cfg(unix)]
[716](https://docs.rs#716)    /// assert!(Utf8Path::from_path(non_unicode_path).is_none(), "non-Unicode path failed");
[717](https://docs.rs#717)    /// ```
[718](https://docs.rs#718)    pub fn from_path(path: &Path) -> Option<&Utf8Path> {
[719](https://docs.rs#719)        path.as_os_str().to_str().map(Utf8Path::new)
[720](https://docs.rs#720)    }

[892](https://docs.rs#892)    /// ```

[896](https://docs.rs#896)        self.0.has_root()
[897](https://docs.rs#897)    }

[901](https://docs.rs#901)    /// Returns [`None`] if the path terminates in a root or prefix.
[902](https://docs.rs#902)    ///
[903](https://docs.rs#903)    /// # Examples
[904](https://docs.rs#904)    ///
[905](https://docs.rs#905)    /// ```
[906](https://docs.rs#906)    /// use camino::Utf8Path;
[907](https://docs.rs#907)    ///
[908](https://docs.rs#908)    /// let path = Utf8Path::new("/foo/bar");
[909](https://docs.rs#909)    /// let parent = path.parent().unwrap();
[910](https://docs.rs#910)    /// assert_eq!(parent, Utf8Path::new("/foo"));
[911](https://docs.rs#911)    ///
[912](https://docs.rs#912)    /// let grand_parent = parent.parent().unwrap();
[913](https://docs.rs#913)    /// assert_eq!(grand_parent, Utf8Path::new("/"));
[914](https://docs.rs#914)    /// assert_eq!(grand_parent.parent(), None);
[915](https://docs.rs#915)    /// ```
[916](https://docs.rs#916)    #[inline]

[918](https://docs.rs#918)    pub fn parent(&self) -> Option<&Utf8Path> {
[919](https://docs.rs#919)        self.0.parent().map(|path| {
[920](https://docs.rs#920)            // SAFETY: self is valid UTF-8, so parent is valid UTF-8 as well
[921](https://docs.rs#921)            unsafe { Utf8Path::assume_utf8(path) }
[922](https://docs.rs#922)        })
[923](https://docs.rs#923)    }

[925](https://docs.rs#925)    /// Produces an iterator over [`Utf8Path`] and its ancestors.
[926](https://docs.rs#926)    ///
[927](https://docs.rs#927)    /// The iterator will yield the [`Utf8Path`] that is returned if the [`parent`] method is used zero
[928](https://docs.rs#928)    /// or more times. That means, the iterator will yield `&self`, `&self.parent().unwrap()`,
[929](https://docs.rs#929)    /// `&self.parent().unwrap().parent().unwrap()` and so on. If the [`parent`] method returns
[930](https://docs.rs#930)    /// [`None`], the iterator will do likewise. The iterator will always yield at least one value,
[931](https://docs.rs#931)    /// namely `&self`.
[932](https://docs.rs#932)    ///
[933](https://docs.rs#933)    /// # Examples
[934](https://docs.rs#934)    ///
[935](https://docs.rs#935)    /// ```
[936](https://docs.rs#936)    /// use camino::Utf8Path;
[937](https://docs.rs#937)    ///
[938](https://docs.rs#938)    /// let mut ancestors = Utf8Path::new("/foo/bar").ancestors();
[939](https://docs.rs#939)    /// assert_eq!(ancestors.next(), Some(Utf8Path::new("/foo/bar")));
[940](https://docs.rs#940)    /// assert_eq!(ancestors.next(), Some(Utf8Path::new("/foo")));
[941](https://docs.rs#941)    /// assert_eq!(ancestors.next(), Some(Utf8Path::new("/")));
[942](https://docs.rs#942)    /// assert_eq!(ancestors.next(), None);
[943](https://docs.rs#943)    ///
[944](https://docs.rs#944)    /// let mut ancestors = Utf8Path::new("../foo/bar").ancestors();
[945](https://docs.rs#945)    /// assert_eq!(ancestors.next(), Some(Utf8Path::new("../foo/bar")));
[946](https://docs.rs#946)    /// assert_eq!(ancestors.next(), Some(Utf8Path::new("../foo")));
[947](https://docs.rs#947)    /// assert_eq!(ancestors.next(), Some(Utf8Path::new("..")));
[948](https://docs.rs#948)    /// assert_eq!(ancestors.next(), Some(Utf8Path::new("")));
[949](https://docs.rs#949)    /// assert_eq!(ancestors.next(), None);
[950](https://docs.rs#950)    /// ```
[951](https://docs.rs#951)    ///
[952](https://docs.rs#952)    /// [`parent`]: Utf8Path::parent
[953](https://docs.rs#953)    #[inline]
[954](https://docs.rs#954)    pub fn ancestors(&self) -> Utf8Ancestors<'_> {
[955](https://docs.rs#955)        Utf8Ancestors(self.0.ancestors())
[956](https://docs.rs#956)    }

[958](https://docs.rs#958)    /// Returns the final component of the [`Utf8Path`], if there is one.
[959](https://docs.rs#959)    ///
[960](https://docs.rs#960)    /// If the path is a normal file, this is the file name. If it's the path of a directory, this
[961](https://docs.rs#961)    /// is the directory name.
[962](https://docs.rs#962)    ///
[963](https://docs.rs#963)    /// Returns [`None`] if the path terminates in `..`.
[964](https://docs.rs#964)    ///
[965](https://docs.rs#965)    /// # Examples
[966](https://docs.rs#966)    ///
[967](https://docs.rs#967)    /// ```
[968](https://docs.rs#968)    /// use camino::Utf8Path;
[969](https://docs.rs#969)    ///
[970](https://docs.rs#970)    /// assert_eq!(Some("bin"), Utf8Path::new("/usr/bin/").file_name());
[971](https://docs.rs#971)    /// assert_eq!(Some("foo.txt"), Utf8Path::new("tmp/foo.txt").file_name());
[972](https://docs.rs#972)    /// assert_eq!(Some("foo.txt"), Utf8Path::new("foo.txt/.").file_name());
[973](https://docs.rs#973)    /// assert_eq!(Some("foo.txt"), Utf8Path::new("foo.txt/.//").file_name());
[974](https://docs.rs#974)    /// assert_eq!(None, Utf8Path::new("foo.txt/..").file_name());
[975](https://docs.rs#975)    /// assert_eq!(None, Utf8Path::new("/").file_name());
[976](https://docs.rs#976)    /// ```
[977](https://docs.rs#977)    #[inline]
[978](https://docs.rs#978)    #[must_use]
[979](https://docs.rs#979)    pub fn file_name(&self) -> Option<&str> {
[980](https://docs.rs#980)        self.0.file_name().map(|s| {
[981](https://docs.rs#981)            // SAFETY: self is valid UTF-8, so file_name is valid UTF-8 as well
[982](https://docs.rs#982)            unsafe { str_assume_utf8(s) }
[983](https://docs.rs#983)        })
[984](https://docs.rs#984)    }

[986](https://docs.rs#986)    /// Returns a path that, when joined onto `base`, yields `self`.
[987](https://docs.rs#987)    ///
[988](https://docs.rs#988)    /// # Errors
[989](https://docs.rs#989)    ///
[990](https://docs.rs#990)    /// If `base` is not a prefix of `self` (i.e., [`starts_with`]
[991](https://docs.rs#991)    /// returns `false`), returns [`Err`].
[992](https://docs.rs#992)    ///
[993](https://docs.rs#993)    /// [`starts_with`]: Utf8Path::starts_with
[994](https://docs.rs#994)    ///
[995](https://docs.rs#995)    /// # Examples
[996](https://docs.rs#996)    ///
[997](https://docs.rs#997)    /// ```
[998](https://docs.rs#998)    /// use camino::{Utf8Path, Utf8PathBuf};
[999](https://docs.rs#999)    ///
[1000](https://docs.rs#1000)    /// let path = Utf8Path::new("/test/haha/foo.txt");
[1001](https://docs.rs#1001)    ///
[1002](https://docs.rs#1002)    /// assert_eq!(path.strip_prefix("/"), Ok(Utf8Path::new("test/haha/foo.txt")));
[1003](https://docs.rs#1003)    /// assert_eq!(path.strip_prefix("/test"), Ok(Utf8Path::new("haha/foo.txt")));
[1004](https://docs.rs#1004)    /// assert_eq!(path.strip_prefix("/test/"), Ok(Utf8Path::new("haha/foo.txt")));
[1005](https://docs.rs#1005)    /// assert_eq!(path.strip_prefix("/test/haha/foo.txt"), Ok(Utf8Path::new("")));
[1006](https://docs.rs#1006)    /// assert_eq!(path.strip_prefix("/test/haha/foo.txt/"), Ok(Utf8Path::new("")));
[1007](https://docs.rs#1007)    ///
[1008](https://docs.rs#1008)    /// assert!(path.strip_prefix("test").is_err());
[1009](https://docs.rs#1009)    /// assert!(path.strip_prefix("/haha").is_err());
[1010](https://docs.rs#1010)    ///
[1011](https://docs.rs#1011)    /// let prefix = Utf8PathBuf::from("/test/");

[1015](https://docs.rs#1015)    pub fn strip_prefix(&self, base: impl AsRef<Path>) -> Result<&Utf8Path, StripPrefixError> {
[1016](https://docs.rs#1016)        self.0.strip_prefix(base).map(|path| {
[1017](https://docs.rs#1017)            // SAFETY: self is valid UTF-8, and strip_prefix returns a part of self (or an empty
[1018](https://docs.rs#1018)            // string), so it is valid UTF-8 as well.
[1019](https://docs.rs#1019)            unsafe { Utf8Path::assume_utf8(path) }
[1020](https://docs.rs#1020)        })
[1021](https://docs.rs#1021)    }

[1267](https://docs.rs#1267)    /// Produces an iterator over the [`Utf8Component`]s of the path.
[1268](https://docs.rs#1268)    ///
[1269](https://docs.rs#1269)    /// When parsing the path, there is a small amount of normalization:
[1270](https://docs.rs#1270)    ///
[1271](https://docs.rs#1271)    /// * Repeated separators are ignored, so `a/b` and `a//b` both have
[1272](https://docs.rs#1272)    ///   `a` and `b` as components.
[1273](https://docs.rs#1273)    ///
[1274](https://docs.rs#1274)    /// * Occurrences of `.` are normalized away, except if they are at the
[1275](https://docs.rs#1275)    ///   beginning of the path. For example, `a/./b`, `a/b/`, `a/b/.` and
[1276](https://docs.rs#1276)    ///   `a/b` all have `a` and `b` as components, but `./a/b` starts with
[1277](https://docs.rs#1277)    ///   an additional [`CurDir`] component.
[1278](https://docs.rs#1278)    ///
[1279](https://docs.rs#1279)    /// * A trailing slash is normalized away, `/a/b` and `/a/b/` are equivalent.
[1280](https://docs.rs#1280)    ///
[1281](https://docs.rs#1281)    /// Note that no other normalization takes place; in particular, `a/c`
[1282](https://docs.rs#1282)    /// and `a/b/../c` are distinct, to account for the possibility that `b`
[1283](https://docs.rs#1283)    /// is a symbolic link (so its parent isn't `a`).
[1284](https://docs.rs#1284)    ///
[1285](https://docs.rs#1285)    /// # Examples
[1286](https://docs.rs#1286)    ///
[1287](https://docs.rs#1287)    /// ```
[1288](https://docs.rs#1288)    /// use camino::{Utf8Component, Utf8Path};
[1289](https://docs.rs#1289)    ///
[1290](https://docs.rs#1290)    /// let mut components = Utf8Path::new("/tmp/foo.txt").components();
[1291](https://docs.rs#1291)    ///
[1292](https://docs.rs#1292)    /// assert_eq!(components.next(), Some(Utf8Component::RootDir));
[1293](https://docs.rs#1293)    /// assert_eq!(components.next(), Some(Utf8Component::Normal("tmp")));
[1294](https://docs.rs#1294)    /// assert_eq!(components.next(), Some(Utf8Component::Normal("foo.txt")));
[1295](https://docs.rs#1295)    /// assert_eq!(components.next(), None)
[1296](https://docs.rs#1296)    /// ```
[1297](https://docs.rs#1297)    ///
[1298](https://docs.rs#1298)    /// [`CurDir`]: Utf8Component::CurDir
[1299](https://docs.rs#1299)    #[inline]
[1300](https://docs.rs#1300)    pub fn components(&self) -> Utf8Components<'_> {
[1301](https://docs.rs#1301)        Utf8Components(self.0.components())
[1302](https://docs.rs#1302)    }
[1303](https://docs.rs#1303)
[1304](https://docs.rs#1304)    /// Produces an iterator over the path's components viewed as [`str`]
[1305](https://docs.rs#1305)    /// slices.
[1306](https://docs.rs#1306)    ///
[1307](https://docs.rs#1307)    /// For more information about the particulars of how the path is separated
[1308](https://docs.rs#1308)    /// into components, see [`components`].
[1309](https://docs.rs#1309)    ///
[1310](https://docs.rs#1310)    /// [`components`]: Utf8Path::components
[1311](https://docs.rs#1311)    ///
[1312](https://docs.rs#1312)    /// # Examples
[1313](https://docs.rs#1313)    ///
[1314](https://docs.rs#1314)    /// ```
[1315](https://docs.rs#1315)    /// use camino::Utf8Path;
[1316](https://docs.rs#1316)    ///
[1317](https://docs.rs#1317)    /// let mut it = Utf8Path::new("/tmp/foo.txt").iter();
[1318](https://docs.rs#1318)    /// assert_eq!(it.next(), Some(std::path::MAIN_SEPARATOR.to_string().as_str()));
[1319](https://docs.rs#1319)    /// assert_eq!(it.next(), Some("tmp"));
[1320](https://docs.rs#1320)    /// assert_eq!(it.next(), Some("foo.txt"));
[1321](https://docs.rs#1321)    /// assert_eq!(it.next(), None)
[1322](https://docs.rs#1322)    /// ```
[1323](https://docs.rs#1323)    #[inline]
[1324](https://docs.rs#1324)    pub fn iter(&self) -> Iter<'_> {
[1325](https://docs.rs#1325)        Iter {
[1326](https://docs.rs#1326)            inner: self.components(),
[1327](https://docs.rs#1327)        }

[1392](https://docs.rs#1392)    /// Returns the canonical, absolute form of the path with all intermediate
[1393](https://docs.rs#1393)    /// components normalized and symbolic links resolved.
[1394](https://docs.rs#1394)    ///
[1395](https://docs.rs#1395)    /// This method attempts to convert the resulting [`PathBuf`] into a [`Utf8PathBuf`]. For a
[1396](https://docs.rs#1396)    /// version that does not attempt to do this conversion, see
[1397](https://docs.rs#1397)    /// [`canonicalize`](Self::canonicalize).
[1398](https://docs.rs#1398)    ///
[1399](https://docs.rs#1399)    /// # Errors
[1400](https://docs.rs#1400)    ///
[1401](https://docs.rs#1401)    /// The I/O operation may return an error: see the [`fs::canonicalize`]
[1402](https://docs.rs#1402)    /// documentation for more.
[1403](https://docs.rs#1403)    ///
[1404](https://docs.rs#1404)    /// If the resulting path is not UTF-8, an [`io::Error`] is returned with the
[1405](https://docs.rs#1405)    /// [`ErrorKind`](io::ErrorKind) set to [`InvalidData`](io::ErrorKind::InvalidData)
[1406](https://docs.rs#1406)    /// and the payload set to a [`FromPathBufError`].
[1407](https://docs.rs#1407)    ///
[1408](https://docs.rs#1408)    /// # Examples
[1409](https://docs.rs#1409)    ///
[1410](https://docs.rs#1410)    /// ```no_run

[1414](https://docs.rs#1414)    /// assert_eq!(path.canonicalize_utf8().unwrap(), Utf8PathBuf::from("/foo/test/bar.rs"));
[1415](https://docs.rs#1415)    /// ```
[1416](https://docs.rs#1416)    pub fn canonicalize_utf8(&self) -> io::Result<Utf8PathBuf> {
[1417](https://docs.rs#1417)        self.canonicalize()
[1418](https://docs.rs#1418)            .and_then(|path| path.try_into().map_err(FromPathBufError::into_io_error))
[1419](https://docs.rs#1419)    }

[1524](https://docs.rs#1524)    /// Returns `true` if the path points at an existing entity.
[1525](https://docs.rs#1525)    ///
[1526](https://docs.rs#1526)    /// Warning: this method may be error-prone, consider using [`try_exists()`] instead!
[1527](https://docs.rs#1527)    /// It also has a risk of introducing time-of-check to time-of-use (TOCTOU) bugs.
[1528](https://docs.rs#1528)    ///
[1529](https://docs.rs#1529)    /// This function will traverse symbolic links to query information about the
[1530](https://docs.rs#1530)    /// destination file. In case of broken symbolic links this will return `false`.
[1531](https://docs.rs#1531)    ///
[1532](https://docs.rs#1532)    /// If you cannot access the directory containing the file, e.g., because of a
[1533](https://docs.rs#1533)    /// permission error, this will return `false`.
[1534](https://docs.rs#1534)    ///
[1535](https://docs.rs#1535)    /// # Examples
[1536](https://docs.rs#1536)    ///
[1537](https://docs.rs#1537)    /// ```no_run
[1538](https://docs.rs#1538)    /// use camino::Utf8Path;
[1539](https://docs.rs#1539)    /// assert!(!Utf8Path::new("does_not_exist.txt").exists());
[1540](https://docs.rs#1540)    /// ```
[1541](https://docs.rs#1541)    ///
[1542](https://docs.rs#1542)    /// # See Also
[1543](https://docs.rs#1543)    ///
[1544](https://docs.rs#1544)    /// This is a convenience function that coerces errors to false. If you want to
[1545](https://docs.rs#1545)    /// check errors, call [`fs::metadata`].
[1546](https://docs.rs#1546)    ///
[1547](https://docs.rs#1547)    /// [`try_exists()`]: Self::try_exists
[1548](https://docs.rs#1548)    #[must_use]
[1549](https://docs.rs#1549)    #[inline]
[1550](https://docs.rs#1550)    pub fn exists(&self) -> bool {
[1551](https://docs.rs#1551)        self.0.exists()
[1552](https://docs.rs#1552)    }
[1553](https://docs.rs#1553)
[1554](https://docs.rs#1554)    /// Returns `Ok(true)` if the path points at an existing entity.
[1555](https://docs.rs#1555)    ///
[1556](https://docs.rs#1556)    /// This function will traverse symbolic links to query information about the
[1557](https://docs.rs#1557)    /// destination file. In case of broken symbolic links this will return `Ok(false)`.
[1558](https://docs.rs#1558)    ///
[1559](https://docs.rs#1559)    /// As opposed to the [`exists()`] method, this one doesn't silently ignore errors
[1560](https://docs.rs#1560)    /// unrelated to the path not existing. (E.g. it will return [`Err`] in case of permission
[1561](https://docs.rs#1561)    /// denied on some of the parent directories.)
[1562](https://docs.rs#1562)    ///
[1563](https://docs.rs#1563)    /// Note that while this avoids some pitfalls of the `exists()` method, it still can not
[1564](https://docs.rs#1564)    /// prevent time-of-check to time-of-use (TOCTOU) bugs. You should only use it in scenarios
[1565](https://docs.rs#1565)    /// where those bugs are not an issue.
[1566](https://docs.rs#1566)    ///
[1567](https://docs.rs#1567)    /// # Examples
[1568](https://docs.rs#1568)    ///
[1569](https://docs.rs#1569)    /// ```no_run
[1570](https://docs.rs#1570)    /// use camino::Utf8Path;
[1571](https://docs.rs#1571)    /// assert!(
[1572](https://docs.rs#1572)    ///     !Utf8Path::new("does_not_exist.txt")
[1573](https://docs.rs#1573)    ///         .try_exists()
[1574](https://docs.rs#1574)    ///         .expect("Can't check existence of file does_not_exist.txt")
[1575](https://docs.rs#1575)    /// );
[1576](https://docs.rs#1576)    /// assert!(Utf8Path::new("/root/secret_file.txt").try_exists().is_err());
[1577](https://docs.rs#1577)    /// ```
[1578](https://docs.rs#1578)    ///
[1579](https://docs.rs#1579)    /// [`exists()`]: Self::exists
[1580](https://docs.rs#1580)    #[inline]
[1581](https://docs.rs#1581)    pub fn try_exists(&self) -> io::Result<bool> {
[1582](https://docs.rs#1582)        match fs::metadata(self) {
[1583](https://docs.rs#1583)            Ok(_) => Ok(true),
[1584](https://docs.rs#1584)            Err(error) if error.kind() == io::ErrorKind::NotFound => Ok(false),
[1585](https://docs.rs#1585)            Err(error) => Err(error),
[1586](https://docs.rs#1586)        }
[1587](https://docs.rs#1587)    }
[1588](https://docs.rs#1588)
[1589](https://docs.rs#1589)    /// Returns `true` if the path exists on disk and is pointing at a regular file.

[1592](https://docs.rs#1592)    /// destination file. In case of broken symbolic links this will return `false`.
[1593](https://docs.rs#1593)    ///
[1594](https://docs.rs#1594)    /// If you cannot access the directory containing the file, e.g., because of a

[1597](https://docs.rs#1597)    /// # Examples
[1598](https://docs.rs#1598)    ///
[1599](https://docs.rs#1599)    /// ```no_run
[1600](https://docs.rs#1600)    /// use camino::Utf8Path;

[1607](https://docs.rs#1607)    /// This is a convenience function that coerces errors to false. If you want to
[1608](https://docs.rs#1608)    /// check errors, call [`fs::metadata`] and handle its [`Result`]. Then call
[1609](https://docs.rs#1609)    /// [`fs::Metadata::is_file`] if it was [`Ok`].
[1610](https://docs.rs#1610)    ///
[1611](https://docs.rs#1611)    /// When the goal is simply to read from (or write to) the source, the most
[1612](https://docs.rs#1612)    /// reliable way to test the source can be read (or written to) is to open
[1613](https://docs.rs#1613)    /// it. Only using `is_file` can break workflows like `diff <( prog_a )` on
[1614](https://docs.rs#1614)    /// a Unix-like system for example. See [`fs::File::open`] or
[1615](https://docs.rs#1615)    /// [`fs::OpenOptions::open`] for more information.
[1616](https://docs.rs#1616)    #[must_use]
[1617](https://docs.rs#1617)    #[inline]

[1652](https://docs.rs#1652)    /// In case of a broken symbolic link this will also return true.
[1653](https://docs.rs#1653)    ///
[1654](https://docs.rs#1654)    /// If you cannot access the directory containing the file, e.g., because of a
[1655](https://docs.rs#1655)    /// permission error, this will return false.
[1656](https://docs.rs#1656)    ///
[1657](https://docs.rs#1657)    /// # Examples
[1658](https://docs.rs#1658)    ///
[1659](https://docs.rs#1659)    #[cfg_attr(unix, doc = "```no_run")]
[1660](https://docs.rs#1660)    #[cfg_attr(not(unix), doc = "```ignore")]
[1661](https://docs.rs#1661)    /// use camino::Utf8Path;
[1662](https://docs.rs#1662)    /// use std::os::unix::fs::symlink;
[1663](https://docs.rs#1663)    ///
[1664](https://docs.rs#1664)    /// let link_path = Utf8Path::new("link");
[1665](https://docs.rs#1665)    /// symlink("/origin_does_not_exist/", link_path).unwrap();
[1666](https://docs.rs#1666)    /// assert_eq!(link_path.is_symlink(), true);
[1667](https://docs.rs#1667)    /// assert_eq!(link_path.exists(), false);
[1668](https://docs.rs#1668)    /// ```
[1669](https://docs.rs#1669)    ///
[1670](https://docs.rs#1670)    /// # See Also
[1671](https://docs.rs#1671)    ///
[1672](https://docs.rs#1672)    /// This is a convenience function that coerces errors to false. If you want to
[1673](https://docs.rs#1673)    /// check errors, call [`Utf8Path::symlink_metadata`] and handle its [`Result`]. Then call
[1674](https://docs.rs#1674)    /// [`fs::Metadata::is_symlink`] if it was [`Ok`].
[1675](https://docs.rs#1675)    #[must_use]
[1676](https://docs.rs#1676)    pub fn is_symlink(&self) -> bool {
[1677](https://docs.rs#1677)        self.symlink_metadata()
[1678](https://docs.rs#1678)            .map(|m| m.file_type().is_symlink())
[1679](https://docs.rs#1679)            .unwrap_or(false)
[1680](https://docs.rs#1680)    }

[1682](https://docs.rs#1682)    /// Converts a [`Box<Utf8Path>`] into a [`Utf8PathBuf`] without copying or allocating.

[1685](https://docs.rs#1685)    pub fn into_path_buf(self: Box<Utf8Path>) -> Utf8PathBuf {
[1686](https://docs.rs#1686)        Utf8PathBuf(self.into_std_boxed_path().into_path_buf())
[1687](https://docs.rs#1687)    }

[1689](https://docs.rs#1689)    // NOTE: `From<Box<Utf8Path>> for Box<Path>` is available, but doesn't render
[1690](https://docs.rs#1690)    // due to a rustdoc bug similar to
[1691](https://docs.rs#1691)    // https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/82465. That's why we don't link it in the doc
[1692](https://docs.rs#1692)    // comment below.
[1693](https://docs.rs#1693)    /// Converts a [`Box<Utf8Path>`] into a [`Box<Path>`] without copying or allocating.
[1694](https://docs.rs#1694)    ///
[1695](https://docs.rs#1695)    /// This is equivalent to the `From<Box<Utf8Path>> for Box<Path>` implementation,
[1696](https://docs.rs#1696)    /// but may aid in type inference.
[1697](https://docs.rs#1697)    ///
[1698](https://docs.rs#1698)    /// # Examples
[1699](https://docs.rs#1699)    ///
[1700](https://docs.rs#1700)    /// ```
[1701](https://docs.rs#1701)    /// use camino::{Utf8Path, Utf8PathBuf};
[1702](https://docs.rs#1702)    /// use std::path::Path;
[1703](https://docs.rs#1703)    ///
[1704](https://docs.rs#1704)    /// let utf8_path_buf = Utf8PathBuf::from("foo.txt");
[1705](https://docs.rs#1705)    /// let boxed_utf8_path = utf8_path_buf.into_boxed_path();
[1706](https://docs.rs#1706)    /// let boxed_std_path = boxed_utf8_path.into_std_boxed_path();
[1707](https://docs.rs#1707)    /// assert_eq!(boxed_std_path.to_str(), Some("foo.txt"));
[1708](https://docs.rs#1708)    ///
[1709](https://docs.rs#1709)    /// // Convert back to a Box<Utf8Path>.
[1710](https://docs.rs#1710)    /// let new_boxed_utf8_path = Utf8Path::from_boxed_path(boxed_std_path).unwrap();
[1711](https://docs.rs#1711)    /// assert_eq!(&*new_boxed_utf8_path, Utf8Path::new("foo.txt"));
[1712](https://docs.rs#1712)    /// ```
[1713](https://docs.rs#1713)    #[must_use = "`self` will be dropped if the result is not used"]
[1714](https://docs.rs#1714)    #[inline]
[1715](https://docs.rs#1715)    pub fn into_std_boxed_path(self: Box<Utf8Path>) -> Box<Path> {
[1716](https://docs.rs#1716)        let ptr = Box::into_raw(self) as *mut Path;
[1717](https://docs.rs#1717)        // SAFETY:
[1718](https://docs.rs#1718)        // * ptr was constructed by consuming self so it represents an owned path.
[1719](https://docs.rs#1719)        // * Utf8Path is marked as #[repr(transparent)] so the conversion from a *mut Utf8Path to a
[1720](https://docs.rs#1720)        //   *mut Path is valid.
[1721](https://docs.rs#1721)        unsafe { Box::from_raw(ptr) }
[1722](https://docs.rs#1722)    }
[1723](https://docs.rs#1723)
[1724](https://docs.rs#1724)    /// Creates a new [`Box<Utf8Path>`] from a [`Box<Path>`] containing valid UTF-8 characters,
[1725](https://docs.rs#1725)    /// without copying or allocating.
[1726](https://docs.rs#1726)    ///
[1727](https://docs.rs#1727)    /// Errors with the original [`Box<Path>`] if it is not valid UTF-8.
[1728](https://docs.rs#1728)    ///
[1729](https://docs.rs#1729)    /// For a version that returns a type that implements [`std::error::Error`],
[1730](https://docs.rs#1730)    /// see [`TryFrom<Box<Path>>`][tryfrom].
[1731](https://docs.rs#1731)    ///
[1732](https://docs.rs#1732)    /// [tryfrom]: #impl-TryFrom<Box<Path>>-for-Box<Utf8Path>
[1733](https://docs.rs#1733)    ///
[1734](https://docs.rs#1734)    /// # Examples
[1735](https://docs.rs#1735)    ///
[1736](https://docs.rs#1736)    /// ```
[1737](https://docs.rs#1737)    /// use camino::Utf8Path;
[1738](https://docs.rs#1738)    /// use std::ffi::OsStr;
[1739](https://docs.rs#1739)    /// # #[cfg(unix)]
[1740](https://docs.rs#1740)    /// use std::os::unix::ffi::OsStrExt;
[1741](https://docs.rs#1741)    /// use std::path::Path;
[1742](https://docs.rs#1742)    ///
[1743](https://docs.rs#1743)    /// let unicode_path: Box<Path> = Path::new("/valid/unicode").into();
[1744](https://docs.rs#1744)    /// Utf8Path::from_boxed_path(unicode_path).expect("valid Unicode path succeeded");
[1745](https://docs.rs#1745)    ///
[1746](https://docs.rs#1746)    /// // Paths on Unix can be non-UTF-8.
[1747](https://docs.rs#1747)    /// # #[cfg(unix)]
[1748](https://docs.rs#1748)    /// let non_unicode_str = OsStr::from_bytes(b"\xFF\xFF\xFF");
[1749](https://docs.rs#1749)    /// # #[cfg(unix)]
[1750](https://docs.rs#1750)    /// let non_unicode_path: Box<Path> = Path::new(non_unicode_str).into();
[1751](https://docs.rs#1751)    /// # #[cfg(unix)]
[1752](https://docs.rs#1752)    /// Utf8Path::from_boxed_path(non_unicode_path).expect_err("non-Unicode path failed");
[1753](https://docs.rs#1753)    /// ```
[1754](https://docs.rs#1754)    pub fn from_boxed_path(path: Box<Path>) -> Result<Box<Utf8Path>, Box<Path>> {
[1755](https://docs.rs#1755)        if path.as_os_str().to_str().is_some() {
[1756](https://docs.rs#1756)            let ptr = Box::into_raw(path) as *mut Utf8Path;
[1757](https://docs.rs#1757)            // SAFETY:
[1758](https://docs.rs#1758)            // * path is valid UTF-8 (just checked above)
[1759](https://docs.rs#1759)            // * ptr was constructed by consuming path so it represents an owned path.
[1760](https://docs.rs#1760)            // * Utf8Path is marked as #[repr(transparent)] so the conversion from a *mut Path to a
[1761](https://docs.rs#1761)            //   *mut Utf8Path is valid.
[1762](https://docs.rs#1762)            Ok(unsafe { Box::from_raw(ptr) })
[1763](https://docs.rs#1763)        } else {
[1764](https://docs.rs#1764)            Err(path)
[1765](https://docs.rs#1765)        }
[1766](https://docs.rs#1766)    }
[1767](https://docs.rs#1767)
[1768](https://docs.rs#1768)    // invariant: Path must be guaranteed to be utf-8 data
[1769](https://docs.rs#1769)    #[inline]
[1770](https://docs.rs#1770)    unsafe fn assume_utf8(path: &Path) -> &Utf8Path {
[1771](https://docs.rs#1771)        // SAFETY: Utf8Path is marked as #[repr(transparent)] so the conversion from a
[1772](https://docs.rs#1772)        // *const Path to a *const Utf8Path is valid.
[1773](https://docs.rs#1773)        &*(path as *const Path as *const Utf8Path)
[1774](https://docs.rs#1774)    }
[1775](https://docs.rs#1775)
[1776](https://docs.rs#1776)    #[cfg(path_buf_deref_mut)]
[1777](https://docs.rs#1777)    #[inline]
[1778](https://docs.rs#1778)    unsafe fn assume_utf8_mut(path: &mut Path) -> &mut Utf8Path {
[1779](https://docs.rs#1779)        &mut *(path as *mut Path as *mut Utf8Path)
[1780](https://docs.rs#1780)    }

[2051](https://docs.rs#2051)
[2052](https://docs.rs#2052)/// A single component of a path.
[2053](https://docs.rs#2053)///
[2054](https://docs.rs#2054)/// A [`Utf8Component`] roughly corresponds to a substring between path separators
[2055](https://docs.rs#2055)/// (`/` or `\`).
[2056](https://docs.rs#2056)///
[2057](https://docs.rs#2057)/// This `enum` is created by iterating over [`Utf8Components`], which in turn is
[2058](https://docs.rs#2058)/// created by the [`components`](Utf8Path::components) method on [`Utf8Path`].
[2059](https://docs.rs#2059)///
[2060](https://docs.rs#2060)/// # Examples
[2061](https://docs.rs#2061)///
[2062](https://docs.rs#2062)/// ```rust
[2063](https://docs.rs#2063)/// use camino::{Utf8Component, Utf8Path};
[2064](https://docs.rs#2064)///
[2065](https://docs.rs#2065)/// let path = Utf8Path::new("/tmp/foo/bar.txt");
[2066](https://docs.rs#2066)/// let components = path.components().collect::<Vec<_>>();
[2067](https://docs.rs#2067)/// assert_eq!(&components, &[
[2068](https://docs.rs#2068)///     Utf8Component::RootDir,
[2069](https://docs.rs#2069)///     Utf8Component::Normal("tmp"),
[2070](https://docs.rs#2070)///     Utf8Component::Normal("foo"),
[2071](https://docs.rs#2071)///     Utf8Component::Normal("bar.txt"),
[2072](https://docs.rs#2072)/// ]);
[2073](https://docs.rs#2073)/// ```
[2074](https://docs.rs#2074)#[derive(Copy, Clone, Eq, PartialEq, Hash, Ord, PartialOrd)]
[2075](https://docs.rs#2075)pub enum Utf8Component<'a> {
[2076](https://docs.rs#2076)    /// A Windows path prefix, e.g., `C:` or `\\server\share`.
[2077](https://docs.rs#2077)    ///
[2078](https://docs.rs#2078)    /// There is a large variety of prefix types, see [`Utf8Prefix`]'s documentation
[2079](https://docs.rs#2079)    /// for more.
[2080](https://docs.rs#2080)    ///
[2081](https://docs.rs#2081)    /// Does not occur on Unix.
[2082](https://docs.rs#2082)    Prefix(Utf8PrefixComponent<'a>),
[2083](https://docs.rs#2083)
[2084](https://docs.rs#2084)    /// The root directory component, appears after any prefix and before anything else.
[2085](https://docs.rs#2085)    ///
[2086](https://docs.rs#2086)    /// It represents a separator that designates that a path starts from root.
[2087](https://docs.rs#2087)    RootDir,
[2088](https://docs.rs#2088)
[2089](https://docs.rs#2089)    /// A reference to the current directory, i.e., `.`.
[2090](https://docs.rs#2090)    CurDir,
[2091](https://docs.rs#2091)
[2092](https://docs.rs#2092)    /// A reference to the parent directory, i.e., `..`.
[2093](https://docs.rs#2093)    ParentDir,
[2094](https://docs.rs#2094)
[2095](https://docs.rs#2095)    /// A normal component, e.g., `a` and `b` in `a/b`.
[2096](https://docs.rs#2096)    ///
[2097](https://docs.rs#2097)    /// This variant is the most common one, it represents references to files
[2098](https://docs.rs#2098)    /// or directories.
[2099](https://docs.rs#2099)    Normal(&'a str),
[2100](https://docs.rs#2100)}
[2101](https://docs.rs#2101)
[2102](https://docs.rs#2102)impl<'a> Utf8Component<'a> {
[2103](https://docs.rs#2103)    unsafe fn new(component: Component<'a>) -> Utf8Component<'a> {
[2104](https://docs.rs#2104)        match component {
[2105](https://docs.rs#2105)            Component::Prefix(prefix) => Utf8Component::Prefix(Utf8PrefixComponent(prefix)),
[2106](https://docs.rs#2106)            Component::RootDir => Utf8Component::RootDir,
[2107](https://docs.rs#2107)            Component::CurDir => Utf8Component::CurDir,
[2108](https://docs.rs#2108)            Component::ParentDir => Utf8Component::ParentDir,
[2109](https://docs.rs#2109)            Component::Normal(s) => Utf8Component::Normal(str_assume_utf8(s)),
[2110](https://docs.rs#2110)        }
[2111](https://docs.rs#2111)    }
[2112](https://docs.rs#2112)
[2113](https://docs.rs#2113)    /// Extracts the underlying [`str`] slice.
[2114](https://docs.rs#2114)    ///
[2115](https://docs.rs#2115)    /// # Examples
[2116](https://docs.rs#2116)    ///
[2117](https://docs.rs#2117)    /// ```
[2118](https://docs.rs#2118)    /// use camino::Utf8Path;
[2119](https://docs.rs#2119)    ///
[2120](https://docs.rs#2120)    /// let path = Utf8Path::new("./tmp/foo/bar.txt");
[2121](https://docs.rs#2121)    /// let components: Vec<_> = path.components().map(|comp| comp.as_str()).collect();
[2122](https://docs.rs#2122)    /// assert_eq!(&components, &[".", "tmp", "foo", "bar.txt"]);
[2123](https://docs.rs#2123)    /// ```
[2124](https://docs.rs#2124)    #[must_use]
[2125](https://docs.rs#2125)    #[inline]
[2126](https://docs.rs#2126)    pub fn as_str(&self) -> &'a str {
[2127](https://docs.rs#2127)        // SAFETY: Utf8Component was constructed from a Utf8Path, so it is guaranteed to be
[2128](https://docs.rs#2128)        // valid UTF-8
[2129](https://docs.rs#2129)        unsafe { str_assume_utf8(self.as_os_str()) }
[2130](https://docs.rs#2130)    }
[2131](https://docs.rs#2131)
[2132](https://docs.rs#2132)    /// Extracts the underlying [`OsStr`] slice.
[2133](https://docs.rs#2133)    ///
[2134](https://docs.rs#2134)    /// # Examples
[2135](https://docs.rs#2135)    ///
[2136](https://docs.rs#2136)    /// ```
[2137](https://docs.rs#2137)    /// use camino::Utf8Path;
[2138](https://docs.rs#2138)    ///
[2139](https://docs.rs#2139)    /// let path = Utf8Path::new("./tmp/foo/bar.txt");
[2140](https://docs.rs#2140)    /// let components: Vec<_> = path.components().map(|comp| comp.as_os_str()).collect();
[2141](https://docs.rs#2141)    /// assert_eq!(&components, &[".", "tmp", "foo", "bar.txt"]);
[2142](https://docs.rs#2142)    /// ```
[2143](https://docs.rs#2143)    #[must_use]
[2144](https://docs.rs#2144)    pub fn as_os_str(&self) -> &'a OsStr {
[2145](https://docs.rs#2145)        match *self {
[2146](https://docs.rs#2146)            Utf8Component::Prefix(prefix) => prefix.as_os_str(),
[2147](https://docs.rs#2147)            Utf8Component::RootDir => Component::RootDir.as_os_str(),
[2148](https://docs.rs#2148)            Utf8Component::CurDir => Component::CurDir.as_os_str(),
[2149](https://docs.rs#2149)            Utf8Component::ParentDir => Component::ParentDir.as_os_str(),
[2150](https://docs.rs#2150)            Utf8Component::Normal(s) => OsStr::new(s),
[2151](https://docs.rs#2151)        }
[2152](https://docs.rs#2152)    }

[2194](https://docs.rs#2194)
[2195](https://docs.rs#2195)/// Windows path prefixes, e.g., `C:` or `\\server\share`.
[2196](https://docs.rs#2196)///
[2197](https://docs.rs#2197)/// Windows uses a variety of path prefix styles, including references to drive
[2198](https://docs.rs#2198)/// volumes (like `C:`), network shared folders (like `\\server\share`), and
[2199](https://docs.rs#2199)/// others. In addition, some path prefixes are "verbatim" (i.e., prefixed with
[2200](https://docs.rs#2200)/// `\\?\`), in which case `/` is *not* treated as a separator and essentially
[2201](https://docs.rs#2201)/// no normalization is performed.
[2202](https://docs.rs#2202)///
[2203](https://docs.rs#2203)/// # Examples
[2204](https://docs.rs#2204)///
[2205](https://docs.rs#2205)/// ```
[2206](https://docs.rs#2206)/// use camino::{Utf8Component, Utf8Path, Utf8Prefix};
[2207](https://docs.rs#2207)/// use camino::Utf8Prefix::*;
[2208](https://docs.rs#2208)///
[2209](https://docs.rs#2209)/// fn get_path_prefix(s: &str) -> Utf8Prefix {
[2210](https://docs.rs#2210)///     let path = Utf8Path::new(s);
[2211](https://docs.rs#2211)///     match path.components().next().unwrap() {
[2212](https://docs.rs#2212)///         Utf8Component::Prefix(prefix_component) => prefix_component.kind(),
[2213](https://docs.rs#2213)///         _ => panic!(),
[2214](https://docs.rs#2214)///     }
[2215](https://docs.rs#2215)/// }
[2216](https://docs.rs#2216)///
[2217](https://docs.rs#2217)/// # if cfg!(windows) {
[2218](https://docs.rs#2218)/// assert_eq!(Verbatim("pictures"), get_path_prefix(r"\\?\pictures\kittens"));
[2219](https://docs.rs#2219)/// assert_eq!(VerbatimUNC("server", "share"), get_path_prefix(r"\\?\UNC\server\share"));
[2220](https://docs.rs#2220)/// assert_eq!(VerbatimDisk(b'C'), get_path_prefix(r"\\?\C:\"));
[2221](https://docs.rs#2221)/// assert_eq!(DeviceNS("BrainInterface"), get_path_prefix(r"\\.\BrainInterface"));
[2222](https://docs.rs#2222)/// assert_eq!(UNC("server", "share"), get_path_prefix(r"\\server\share"));
[2223](https://docs.rs#2223)/// assert_eq!(Disk(b'C'), get_path_prefix(r"C:\Users\Rust\Pictures\Ferris"));
[2224](https://docs.rs#2224)/// # }
[2225](https://docs.rs#2225)/// ```
[2226](https://docs.rs#2226)#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, Hash, PartialOrd, Ord, PartialEq, Eq)]
[2227](https://docs.rs#2227)pub enum Utf8Prefix<'a> {
[2228](https://docs.rs#2228)    /// Verbatim prefix, e.g., `\\?\cat_pics`.
[2229](https://docs.rs#2229)    ///
[2230](https://docs.rs#2230)    /// Verbatim prefixes consist of `\\?\` immediately followed by the given
[2231](https://docs.rs#2231)    /// component.
[2232](https://docs.rs#2232)    Verbatim(&'a str),
[2233](https://docs.rs#2233)
[2234](https://docs.rs#2234)    /// Verbatim prefix using Windows' _**U**niform **N**aming **C**onvention_,
[2235](https://docs.rs#2235)    /// e.g., `\\?\UNC\server\share`.
[2236](https://docs.rs#2236)    ///
[2237](https://docs.rs#2237)    /// Verbatim UNC prefixes consist of `\\?\UNC\` immediately followed by the
[2238](https://docs.rs#2238)    /// server's hostname and a share name.
[2239](https://docs.rs#2239)    VerbatimUNC(&'a str, &'a str),
[2240](https://docs.rs#2240)
[2241](https://docs.rs#2241)    /// Verbatim disk prefix, e.g., `\\?\C:`.
[2242](https://docs.rs#2242)    ///
[2243](https://docs.rs#2243)    /// Verbatim disk prefixes consist of `\\?\` immediately followed by the
[2244](https://docs.rs#2244)    /// drive letter and `:`.
[2245](https://docs.rs#2245)    VerbatimDisk(u8),
[2246](https://docs.rs#2246)
[2247](https://docs.rs#2247)    /// Device namespace prefix, e.g., `\\.\COM42`.
[2248](https://docs.rs#2248)    ///
[2249](https://docs.rs#2249)    /// Device namespace prefixes consist of `\\.\` immediately followed by the
[2250](https://docs.rs#2250)    /// device name.
[2251](https://docs.rs#2251)    DeviceNS(&'a str),
[2252](https://docs.rs#2252)
[2253](https://docs.rs#2253)    /// Prefix using Windows' _**U**niform **N**aming **C**onvention_, e.g.
[2254](https://docs.rs#2254)    /// `\\server\share`.
[2255](https://docs.rs#2255)    ///
[2256](https://docs.rs#2256)    /// UNC prefixes consist of the server's hostname and a share name.
[2257](https://docs.rs#2257)    UNC(&'a str, &'a str),
[2258](https://docs.rs#2258)
[2259](https://docs.rs#2259)    /// Prefix `C:` for the given disk drive.
[2260](https://docs.rs#2260)    Disk(u8),
[2261](https://docs.rs#2261)}
[2262](https://docs.rs#2262)
[2263](https://docs.rs#2263)impl Utf8Prefix<'_> {
[2264](https://docs.rs#2264)    /// Determines if the prefix is verbatim, i.e., begins with `\\?\`.
[2265](https://docs.rs#2265)    ///
[2266](https://docs.rs#2266)    /// # Examples
[2267](https://docs.rs#2267)    ///
[2268](https://docs.rs#2268)    /// ```
[2269](https://docs.rs#2269)    /// use camino::Utf8Prefix::*;
[2270](https://docs.rs#2270)    ///
[2271](https://docs.rs#2271)    /// assert!(Verbatim("pictures").is_verbatim());
[2272](https://docs.rs#2272)    /// assert!(VerbatimUNC("server", "share").is_verbatim());
[2273](https://docs.rs#2273)    /// assert!(VerbatimDisk(b'C').is_verbatim());
[2274](https://docs.rs#2274)    /// assert!(!DeviceNS("BrainInterface").is_verbatim());
[2275](https://docs.rs#2275)    /// assert!(!UNC("server", "share").is_verbatim());
[2276](https://docs.rs#2276)    /// assert!(!Disk(b'C').is_verbatim());
[2277](https://docs.rs#2277)    /// ```
[2278](https://docs.rs#2278)    #[must_use]
[2279](https://docs.rs#2279)    pub fn is_verbatim(&self) -> bool {
[2280](https://docs.rs#2280)        use Utf8Prefix::*;
[2281](https://docs.rs#2281)        matches!(self, Verbatim(_) | VerbatimDisk(_) | VerbatimUNC(..))
[2282](https://docs.rs#2282)    }
[2283](https://docs.rs#2283)}
[2284](https://docs.rs#2284)
[2285](https://docs.rs#2285)/// A structure wrapping a Windows path prefix as well as its unparsed string
[2286](https://docs.rs#2286)/// representation.
[2287](https://docs.rs#2287)///
[2288](https://docs.rs#2288)/// In addition to the parsed [`Utf8Prefix`] information returned by [`kind`],
[2289](https://docs.rs#2289)/// [`Utf8PrefixComponent`] also holds the raw and unparsed [`str`] slice,
[2290](https://docs.rs#2290)/// returned by [`as_str`].
[2291](https://docs.rs#2291)///
[2292](https://docs.rs#2292)/// Instances of this `struct` can be obtained by matching against the
[2293](https://docs.rs#2293)/// [`Prefix` variant] on [`Utf8Component`].
[2294](https://docs.rs#2294)///
[2295](https://docs.rs#2295)/// Does not occur on Unix.
[2296](https://docs.rs#2296)///
[2297](https://docs.rs#2297)/// # Examples
[2298](https://docs.rs#2298)///
[2299](https://docs.rs#2299)/// ```
[2300](https://docs.rs#2300)/// # if cfg!(windows) {
[2301](https://docs.rs#2301)/// use camino::{Utf8Component, Utf8Path, Utf8Prefix};
[2302](https://docs.rs#2302)/// use std::ffi::OsStr;
[2303](https://docs.rs#2303)///
[2304](https://docs.rs#2304)/// let path = Utf8Path::new(r"C:\you\later\");
[2305](https://docs.rs#2305)/// match path.components().next().unwrap() {
[2306](https://docs.rs#2306)///     Utf8Component::Prefix(prefix_component) => {
[2307](https://docs.rs#2307)///         assert_eq!(Utf8Prefix::Disk(b'C'), prefix_component.kind());
[2308](https://docs.rs#2308)///         assert_eq!("C:", prefix_component.as_str());
[2309](https://docs.rs#2309)///     }
[2310](https://docs.rs#2310)///     _ => unreachable!(),
[2311](https://docs.rs#2311)/// }
[2312](https://docs.rs#2312)/// # }
[2313](https://docs.rs#2313)/// ```
[2314](https://docs.rs#2314)///
[2315](https://docs.rs#2315)/// [`as_str`]: Utf8PrefixComponent::as_str
[2316](https://docs.rs#2316)/// [`kind`]: Utf8PrefixComponent::kind
[2317](https://docs.rs#2317)/// [`Prefix` variant]: Utf8Component::Prefix
[2318](https://docs.rs#2318)#[repr(transparent)]
[2319](https://docs.rs#2319)#[derive(Clone, Copy, Eq, PartialEq, Hash, Ord, PartialOrd)]
[2320](https://docs.rs#2320)pub struct Utf8PrefixComponent<'a>(PrefixComponent<'a>);
[2321](https://docs.rs#2321)
[2322](https://docs.rs#2322)impl<'a> Utf8PrefixComponent<'a> {
[2323](https://docs.rs#2323)    /// Returns the parsed prefix data.
[2324](https://docs.rs#2324)    ///
[2325](https://docs.rs#2325)    /// See [`Utf8Prefix`]'s documentation for more information on the different
[2326](https://docs.rs#2326)    /// kinds of prefixes.
[2327](https://docs.rs#2327)    #[must_use]
[2328](https://docs.rs#2328)    pub fn kind(&self) -> Utf8Prefix<'a> {
[2329](https://docs.rs#2329)        // SAFETY for all the below unsafe blocks: the path self was originally constructed from was
[2330](https://docs.rs#2330)        // UTF-8 so any parts of it are valid UTF-8
[2331](https://docs.rs#2331)        match self.0.kind() {
[2332](https://docs.rs#2332)            Prefix::Verbatim(prefix) => Utf8Prefix::Verbatim(unsafe { str_assume_utf8(prefix) }),
[2333](https://docs.rs#2333)            Prefix::VerbatimUNC(server, share) => {
[2334](https://docs.rs#2334)                let server = unsafe { str_assume_utf8(server) };
[2335](https://docs.rs#2335)                let share = unsafe { str_assume_utf8(share) };
[2336](https://docs.rs#2336)                Utf8Prefix::VerbatimUNC(server, share)
[2337](https://docs.rs#2337)            }
[2338](https://docs.rs#2338)            Prefix::VerbatimDisk(drive) => Utf8Prefix::VerbatimDisk(drive),
[2339](https://docs.rs#2339)            Prefix::DeviceNS(prefix) => Utf8Prefix::DeviceNS(unsafe { str_assume_utf8(prefix) }),
[2340](https://docs.rs#2340)            Prefix::UNC(server, share) => {
[2341](https://docs.rs#2341)                let server = unsafe { str_assume_utf8(server) };
[2342](https://docs.rs#2342)                let share = unsafe { str_assume_utf8(share) };
[2343](https://docs.rs#2343)                Utf8Prefix::UNC(server, share)
[2344](https://docs.rs#2344)            }
[2345](https://docs.rs#2345)            Prefix::Disk(drive) => Utf8Prefix::Disk(drive),
[2346](https://docs.rs#2346)        }
[2347](https://docs.rs#2347)    }
[2348](https://docs.rs#2348)
[2349](https://docs.rs#2349)    /// Returns the [`str`] slice for this prefix.

[2352](https://docs.rs#2352)    pub fn as_str(&self) -> &'a str {

[2354](https://docs.rs#2354)        // valid UTF-8
[2355](https://docs.rs#2355)        unsafe { str_assume_utf8(self.as_os_str()) }
[2356](https://docs.rs#2356)    }

[2382](https://docs.rs#2382)/// Iterator over the entries in a directory.
[2383](https://docs.rs#2383)///
[2384](https://docs.rs#2384)/// This iterator is returned from [`Utf8Path::read_dir_utf8`] and will yield instances of
[2385](https://docs.rs#2385)/// <code>[io::Result]<[Utf8DirEntry]></code>. Through a [`Utf8DirEntry`] information like the entry's path
[2386](https://docs.rs#2386)/// and possibly other metadata can be learned.
[2387](https://docs.rs#2387)///
[2388](https://docs.rs#2388)/// The order in which this iterator returns entries is platform and filesystem
[2389](https://docs.rs#2389)/// dependent.
[2390](https://docs.rs#2390)///
[2391](https://docs.rs#2391)/// # Errors
[2392](https://docs.rs#2392)///
[2393](https://docs.rs#2393)/// This [`io::Result`] will be an [`Err`] if there's some sort of intermittent
[2394](https://docs.rs#2394)/// IO error during iteration.
[2395](https://docs.rs#2395)///
[2396](https://docs.rs#2396)/// If a directory entry is not UTF-8, an [`io::Error`] is returned with the
[2397](https://docs.rs#2397)/// [`ErrorKind`](io::ErrorKind) set to [`InvalidData`][io::ErrorKind::InvalidData]
[2398](https://docs.rs#2398)/// and the payload set to a [`FromPathBufError`].
[2399](https://docs.rs#2399)#[derive(Debug)]
[2400](https://docs.rs#2400)pub struct ReadDirUtf8 {
[2401](https://docs.rs#2401)    inner: fs::ReadDir,
[2402](https://docs.rs#2402)}

[2417](https://docs.rs#2417)/// entry can be inspected via methods to learn about the full path or possibly other metadata.
[2418](https://docs.rs#2418)#[derive(Debug)]

[2426](https://docs.rs#2426)        let path = inner
[2427](https://docs.rs#2427)            .path()
[2428](https://docs.rs#2428)            .try_into()
[2429](https://docs.rs#2429)            .map_err(|err| io::Error::new(io::ErrorKind::InvalidData, err))?;
[2430](https://docs.rs#2430)        Ok(Self { inner, path })
[2431](https://docs.rs#2431)    }

[2433](https://docs.rs#2433)    /// Returns the full path to the file that this entry represents.
[2434](https://docs.rs#2434)    ///
[2435](https://docs.rs#2435)    /// The full path is created by joining the original path to `read_dir`
[2436](https://docs.rs#2436)    /// with the filename of this entry.
[2437](https://docs.rs#2437)    ///
[2438](https://docs.rs#2438)    /// # Examples
[2439](https://docs.rs#2439)    ///
[2440](https://docs.rs#2440)    /// ```no_run
[2441](https://docs.rs#2441)    /// use camino::Utf8Path;
[2442](https://docs.rs#2442)    ///
[2443](https://docs.rs#2443)    /// fn main() -> std::io::Result<()> {
[2444](https://docs.rs#2444)    ///     for entry in Utf8Path::new(".").read_dir_utf8()? {
[2445](https://docs.rs#2445)    ///         let dir = entry?;
[2446](https://docs.rs#2446)    ///         println!("{}", dir.path());
[2447](https://docs.rs#2447)    ///     }
[2448](https://docs.rs#2448)    ///     Ok(())
[2449](https://docs.rs#2449)    /// }
[2450](https://docs.rs#2450)    /// ```
[2451](https://docs.rs#2451)    ///
[2452](https://docs.rs#2452)    /// This prints output like:
[2453](https://docs.rs#2453)    ///
[2454](https://docs.rs#2454)    /// ```text
[2455](https://docs.rs#2455)    /// ./whatever.txt
[2456](https://docs.rs#2456)    /// ./foo.html
[2457](https://docs.rs#2457)    /// ./hello_world.rs
[2458](https://docs.rs#2458)    /// ```
[2459](https://docs.rs#2459)    ///
[2460](https://docs.rs#2460)    /// The exact text, of course, depends on what files you have in `.`.
[2461](https://docs.rs#2461)    #[inline]
[2462](https://docs.rs#2462)    pub fn path(&self) -> &Utf8Path {
[2463](https://docs.rs#2463)        &self.path
[2464](https://docs.rs#2464)    }
[2465](https://docs.rs#2465)
[2466](https://docs.rs#2466)    /// Returns the metadata for the file that this entry points at.
[2467](https://docs.rs#2467)    ///
[2468](https://docs.rs#2468)    /// This function will not traverse symlinks if this entry points at a symlink. To traverse
[2469](https://docs.rs#2469)    /// symlinks use [`Utf8Path::metadata`] or [`fs::File::metadata`].
[2470](https://docs.rs#2470)    ///
[2471](https://docs.rs#2471)    /// # Platform-specific behavior
[2472](https://docs.rs#2472)    ///
[2473](https://docs.rs#2473)    /// On Windows this function is cheap to call (no extra system calls
[2474](https://docs.rs#2474)    /// needed), but on Unix platforms this function is the equivalent of
[2475](https://docs.rs#2475)    /// calling `symlink_metadata` on the path.
[2476](https://docs.rs#2476)    ///
[2477](https://docs.rs#2477)    /// # Examples
[2478](https://docs.rs#2478)    ///
[2479](https://docs.rs#2479)    /// ```
[2480](https://docs.rs#2480)    /// use camino::Utf8Path;
[2481](https://docs.rs#2481)    ///
[2482](https://docs.rs#2482)    /// if let Ok(entries) = Utf8Path::new(".").read_dir_utf8() {
[2483](https://docs.rs#2483)    ///     for entry in entries {
[2484](https://docs.rs#2484)    ///         if let Ok(entry) = entry {
[2485](https://docs.rs#2485)    ///             // Here, `entry` is a `Utf8DirEntry`.
[2486](https://docs.rs#2486)    ///             if let Ok(metadata) = entry.metadata() {
[2487](https://docs.rs#2487)    ///                 // Now let's show our entry's permissions!
[2488](https://docs.rs#2488)    ///                 println!("{}: {:?}", entry.path(), metadata.permissions());
[2489](https://docs.rs#2489)    ///             } else {
[2490](https://docs.rs#2490)    ///                 println!("Couldn't get metadata for {}", entry.path());
[2491](https://docs.rs#2491)    ///             }
[2492](https://docs.rs#2492)    ///         }
[2493](https://docs.rs#2493)    ///     }
[2494](https://docs.rs#2494)    /// }
[2495](https://docs.rs#2495)    /// ```
[2496](https://docs.rs#2496)    #[inline]
[2497](https://docs.rs#2497)    pub fn metadata(&self) -> io::Result<Metadata> {
[2498](https://docs.rs#2498)        self.inner.metadata()
[2499](https://docs.rs#2499)    }

[2619](https://docs.rs#2619)        let arc: Arc<Path> = Arc::from(AsRef::<Path>::as_ref(path));
[2620](https://docs.rs#2620)        let ptr = Arc::into_raw(arc) as *const Utf8Path;
[2621](https://docs.rs#2621)        // SAFETY:

[2623](https://docs.rs#2623)        // * ptr was created by consuming an Arc<Path> so it represents an arced pointer
[2624](https://docs.rs#2624)        // * Utf8Path is marked as #[repr(transparent)] so the conversion from *const Path to
[2625](https://docs.rs#2625)        //   *const Utf8Path is valid
[2626](https://docs.rs#2626)        unsafe { Arc::from_raw(ptr) }
[2627](https://docs.rs#2627)    }

[2719](https://docs.rs#2719)impl From<Utf8PathBuf> for Arc<Utf8Path> {
[2720](https://docs.rs#2720)    fn from(path: Utf8PathBuf) -> Arc<Utf8Path> {
[2721](https://docs.rs#2721)        let arc: Arc<Path> = Arc::from(path.0);
[2722](https://docs.rs#2722)        let ptr = Arc::into_raw(arc) as *const Utf8Path;
[2723](https://docs.rs#2723)        // SAFETY:
[2724](https://docs.rs#2724)        // * path is valid UTF-8
[2725](https://docs.rs#2725)        // * ptr was created by consuming an Arc<Path> so it represents an arced pointer
[2726](https://docs.rs#2726)        // * Utf8Path is marked as #[repr(transparent)] so the conversion from *const Path to
[2727](https://docs.rs#2727)        //   *const Utf8Path is valid
[2728](https://docs.rs#2728)        unsafe { Arc::from_raw(ptr) }
[2729](https://docs.rs#2729)    }

[2804](https://docs.rs#2804)///
[2805](https://docs.rs#2805)/// # Examples
[2806](https://docs.rs#2806)///
[2807](https://docs.rs#2807)/// ```

[2812](https://docs.rs#2812)/// use std::os::unix::ffi::OsStrExt;
[2813](https://docs.rs#2813)/// use std::path::Path;
[2814](https://docs.rs#2814)///
[2815](https://docs.rs#2815)/// let unicode_path = Path::new("/valid/unicode");

[2817](https://docs.rs#2817)///
[2818](https://docs.rs#2818)/// // Paths on Unix can be non-UTF-8.
[2819](https://docs.rs#2819)/// # #[cfg(unix)]
[2820](https://docs.rs#2820)/// let non_unicode_str = OsStr::from_bytes(b"\xFF\xFF\xFF");
[2821](https://docs.rs#2821)/// # #[cfg(unix)]
[2822](https://docs.rs#2822)/// let non_unicode_path = Path::new(non_unicode_str);
[2823](https://docs.rs#2823)/// # #[cfg(unix)]
[2824](https://docs.rs#2824)/// assert!(<&Utf8Path>::try_from(non_unicode_path).is_err(), "non-Unicode path failed");
[2825](https://docs.rs#2825)/// ```

[2923](https://docs.rs#2923)///     .expect_err("non-Unicode path failed");

[3637](https://docs.rs#3637)
[3638](https://docs.rs#3638)/// Makes the path absolute without accessing the filesystem, converting it to a [`Utf8PathBuf`].
[3639](https://docs.rs#3639)///
[3640](https://docs.rs#3640)/// If the path is relative, the current directory is used as the base directory. All intermediate
[3641](https://docs.rs#3641)/// components will be resolved according to platform-specific rules, but unlike
[3642](https://docs.rs#3642)/// [`canonicalize`][Utf8Path::canonicalize] or [`canonicalize_utf8`](Utf8Path::canonicalize_utf8),
[3643](https://docs.rs#3643)/// this does not resolve symlinks and may succeed even if the path does not exist.
[3644](https://docs.rs#3644)///
[3645](https://docs.rs#3645)/// *Requires Rust 1.79 or newer.*
[3646](https://docs.rs#3646)///
[3647](https://docs.rs#3647)/// # Errors
[3648](https://docs.rs#3648)///
[3649](https://docs.rs#3649)/// Errors if:
[3650](https://docs.rs#3650)///
[3651](https://docs.rs#3651)/// * The path is empty.
[3652](https://docs.rs#3652)/// * The [current directory][std::env::current_dir] cannot be determined.
[3653](https://docs.rs#3653)/// * The path is not valid UTF-8.
[3654](https://docs.rs#3654)///
[3655](https://docs.rs#3655)/// # Examples
[3656](https://docs.rs#3656)///
[3657](https://docs.rs#3657)/// ## POSIX paths
[3658](https://docs.rs#3658)///
[3659](https://docs.rs#3659)/// ```
[3660](https://docs.rs#3660)/// # #[cfg(unix)]
[3661](https://docs.rs#3661)/// fn main() -> std::io::Result<()> {
[3662](https://docs.rs#3662)///     use camino::Utf8Path;
[3663](https://docs.rs#3663)///
[3664](https://docs.rs#3664)///     // Relative to absolute
[3665](https://docs.rs#3665)///     let absolute = camino::absolute_utf8("foo/./bar")?;
[3666](https://docs.rs#3666)///     assert!(absolute.ends_with("foo/bar"));
[3667](https://docs.rs#3667)///
[3668](https://docs.rs#3668)///     // Absolute to absolute
[3669](https://docs.rs#3669)///     let absolute = camino::absolute_utf8("/foo//test/.././bar.rs")?;
[3670](https://docs.rs#3670)///     assert_eq!(absolute, Utf8Path::new("/foo/test/../bar.rs"));
[3671](https://docs.rs#3671)///     Ok(())
[3672](https://docs.rs#3672)/// }
[3673](https://docs.rs#3673)/// # #[cfg(not(unix))]
[3674](https://docs.rs#3674)/// # fn main() {}
[3675](https://docs.rs#3675)/// ```
[3676](https://docs.rs#3676)///
[3677](https://docs.rs#3677)/// The path is resolved using [POSIX semantics][posix-semantics] except that it stops short of
[3678](https://docs.rs#3678)/// resolving symlinks. This means it will keep `..` components and trailing slashes.
[3679](https://docs.rs#3679)///
[3680](https://docs.rs#3680)/// ## Windows paths
[3681](https://docs.rs#3681)///
[3682](https://docs.rs#3682)/// ```
[3683](https://docs.rs#3683)/// # #[cfg(windows)]
[3684](https://docs.rs#3684)/// fn main() -> std::io::Result<()> {
[3685](https://docs.rs#3685)///     use camino::Utf8Path;
[3686](https://docs.rs#3686)///
[3687](https://docs.rs#3687)///     // Relative to absolute
[3688](https://docs.rs#3688)///     let absolute = camino::absolute_utf8("foo/./bar")?;
[3689](https://docs.rs#3689)///     assert!(absolute.ends_with(r"foo\bar"));
[3690](https://docs.rs#3690)///
[3691](https://docs.rs#3691)///     // Absolute to absolute
[3692](https://docs.rs#3692)///     let absolute = camino::absolute_utf8(r"C:\foo//test\..\./bar.rs")?;
[3693](https://docs.rs#3693)///
[3694](https://docs.rs#3694)///     assert_eq!(absolute, Utf8Path::new(r"C:\foo\bar.rs"));
[3695](https://docs.rs#3695)///     Ok(())
[3696](https://docs.rs#3696)/// }
[3697](https://docs.rs#3697)/// # #[cfg(not(windows))]
[3698](https://docs.rs#3698)/// # fn main() {}
[3699](https://docs.rs#3699)/// ```
[3700](https://docs.rs#3700)///
[3701](https://docs.rs#3701)/// For verbatim paths this will simply return the path as given. For other paths this is currently
[3702](https://docs.rs#3702)/// equivalent to calling [`GetFullPathNameW`][windows-path].
[3703](https://docs.rs#3703)///
[3704](https://docs.rs#3704)/// Note that this [may change in the future][changes].
[3705](https://docs.rs#3705)///
[3706](https://docs.rs#3706)/// [changes]: io#platform-specific-behavior
[3707](https://docs.rs#3707)/// [posix-semantics]:
[3708](https://docs.rs#3708)///     https://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/9699919799/basedefs/V1_chap04.html#tag_04_13
[3709](https://docs.rs#3709)/// [windows-path]:
[3710](https://docs.rs#3710)///     https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/fileapi/nf-fileapi-getfullpathnamew
[3711](https://docs.rs#3711)#[cfg(absolute_path)]
[3712](https://docs.rs#3712)pub fn absolute_utf8<P: AsRef<Path>>(path: P) -> io::Result<Utf8PathBuf> {
[3713](https://docs.rs#3713)    // Note that even if the passed in path is valid UTF-8, it is not guaranteed
[3714](https://docs.rs#3714)    // that the absolute path will be valid UTF-8. For example, the current
[3715](https://docs.rs#3715)    // directory may not be valid UTF-8.
[3716](https://docs.rs#3716)    //
[3717](https://docs.rs#3717)    // That's why we take `AsRef<Path>` instead of `AsRef<Utf8Path>` here -- we
[3718](https://docs.rs#3718)    // have to pay the cost of checking for valid UTF-8 anyway.
[3719](https://docs.rs#3719)    let path = path.as_ref();
[3720](https://docs.rs#3720)    #[allow(clippy::incompatible_msrv)]
[3721](https://docs.rs#3721)    Utf8PathBuf::try_from(std::path::absolute(path)?).map_err(|error| error.into_io_error())
[3722](https://docs.rs#3722)}
[3723](https://docs.rs#3723)
[3724](https://docs.rs#3724)// invariant: OsStr must be guaranteed to be utf8 data
[3725](https://docs.rs#3725)#[inline]
[3726](https://docs.rs#3726)unsafe fn str_assume_utf8(string: &OsStr) -> &str {
[3727](https://docs.rs#3727)    #[cfg(os_str_bytes)]
[3728](https://docs.rs#3728)    {
[3729](https://docs.rs#3729)        // SAFETY: OsStr is guaranteed to be utf8 data from the invariant
[3730](https://docs.rs#3730)        unsafe {
[3731](https://docs.rs#3731)            std::str::from_utf8_unchecked(
[3732](https://docs.rs#3732)                #[allow(clippy::incompatible_msrv)]
[3733](https://docs.rs#3733)                string.as_encoded_bytes(),
[3734](https://docs.rs#3734)            )
[3735](https://docs.rs#3735)        }
[3736](https://docs.rs#3736)    }
[3737](https://docs.rs#3737)    #[cfg(not(os_str_bytes))]
[3738](https://docs.rs#3738)    {
[3739](https://docs.rs#3739)        // Adapted from the source code for Option::unwrap_unchecked.
[3740](https://docs.rs#3740)        match string.to_str() {
[3741](https://docs.rs#3741)            Some(val) => val,
[3742](https://docs.rs#3742)            None => std::hint::unreachable_unchecked(),
[3743](https://docs.rs#3743)        }

# Utf8PathBuf in camino - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/camino/1.2.4/camino/struct.Utf8PathBuf.html

`pub struct Utf8PathBuf(/* private fields */);`## Expand description

An owned, mutable UTF-8 path (akin to [ String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)).

This type provides methods like [ push](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8PathBuf.html#method.push) and

[that mutate the path in place. It also implements](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8PathBuf.html#method.set_extension)

`set_extension`[to](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/ops/deref/trait.Deref.html)

`Deref`[, meaning that all methods on](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8Path.html)

`Utf8Path`[slices are available on](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8Path.html)

`Utf8Path`[values as well.](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8PathBuf.html)

`Utf8PathBuf`[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

You can use [ push](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8PathBuf.html#method.push) to build up a

[from components:](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8PathBuf.html)

`Utf8PathBuf````
use camino::Utf8PathBuf;
let mut path = Utf8PathBuf::new();
path.push(r"C:\");
path.push("windows");
path.push("system32");
path.set_extension("dll");
```
However, [ push](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8PathBuf.html#method.push) is best used for dynamic situations. This is a better way
to do this when you know all of the components ahead of time:

```
use camino::Utf8PathBuf;
let path: Utf8PathBuf = [r"C:\", "windows", "system32.dll"].iter().collect();
```
We can still do better than this! Since these are all strings, we can use
[ From::from](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/convert/trait.From.html#tymethod.from):

```
use camino::Utf8PathBuf;
let path = Utf8PathBuf::from(r"C:\windows\system32.dll");
```
Which method works best depends on what kind of situation you’re in.

Consumes and leaks the [ Utf8PathBuf](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8PathBuf.html), returning a mutable reference to the contents,

`&'a mut Utf8Path`.The caller has free choice over the returned lifetime, including ’static. Indeed, this function is ideally used for data that lives for the remainder of the program’s life, as dropping the returned reference will cause a memory leak.

It does not reallocate or shrink the [ Utf8PathBuf](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8PathBuf.html), so the leaked allocation may include
unused capacity that is not part of the returned slice. If you want to discard excess
capacity, call

[, and then](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8PathBuf.html#method.into_boxed_path)

`into_boxed_path`[instead. However, keep in mind that trimming the capacity may result in a reallocation and copy.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/boxed/struct.Box.html#method.leak)

`Box::leak`*Requires Rust 1.89 or newer.*

Extends `self` with `path`.

If `path` is absolute, it replaces the current path.

On Windows:

- if `path`has a root but no prefix (e.g.,`\windows`), it replaces everything except for the prefix (if any) of`self`.
- if `path`has a prefix but no root, it replaces`self`.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-7)Examples

Pushing a relative path extends the existing path:

```
use camino::Utf8PathBuf;
let mut path = Utf8PathBuf::from("/tmp");
path.push("file.bk");
assert_eq!(path, Utf8PathBuf::from("/tmp/file.bk"));
```
Pushing an absolute path replaces the existing path:

```
use camino::Utf8PathBuf;
let mut path = Utf8PathBuf::from("/tmp");
path.push("/etc");
assert_eq!(path, Utf8PathBuf::from("/etc"));
```
Truncates `self` to [ self.parent](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8Path.html#method.parent).

Returns `false` and does nothing if [ self.parent](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8Path.html#method.parent) is

[. Otherwise, returns](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None)

`None``true`.[§](https://docs.rs#examples-8)Examples

```
use camino::{Utf8Path, Utf8PathBuf};
let mut p = Utf8PathBuf::from("/spirited/away.rs");
p.pop();
assert_eq!(Utf8Path::new("/spirited"), p);
p.pop();
assert_eq!(Utf8Path::new("/"), p);
```

[§](https://docs.rs#panics)Panics

Panics if the passed extension contains a path separator (see
[ is_separator](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/path/fn.is_separator.html)).

[§](https://docs.rs#caveats)Caveats

The appended `extension` may contain dots and will be used in its entirety,
but only the part after the final dot will be reflected in [ self.extension](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8Path.html#method.extension).

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/camino/lib.rs.html#854-856)#### pub fn [is_absolute](https://docs.rs#method.is_absolute)(&self) -> [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/camino/lib.rs.html#854-856)

#### pub fn [is_absolute](https://docs.rs#method.is_absolute)(&self) -> [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)

Returns `true` if the [ Utf8Path](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8Path.html) is absolute, i.e., if it is independent of
the current directory.

-
On Unix, a path is absolute if it starts with the root, so `is_absolute`and`has_root`
-
On Windows, a path is absolute if it has a prefix and starts with the root: `C:\windows`is absolute, while`C:temp`and`\temp`are not.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-18)Examples

```
use camino::Utf8Path;
assert!(!Utf8Path::new("foo.txt").is_absolute());
```
Returns `true` if the [ Utf8Path](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8Path.html) has a root.

-
On Unix, a path has a root if it begins with `/`.
-
On Windows, a path has a root if it: - has no prefix and begins with a separator, e.g., `\windows`
- has a prefix followed by a separator, e.g., `C:\windows`but not`C:windows`
- has any non-disk prefix, e.g., `\\server\share`

- has no prefix and begins with a separator, e.g.,

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-20)Examples

```
use camino::Utf8Path;
assert!(Utf8Path::new("/etc/passwd").has_root());
```
Returns the [ Path](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/path/struct.Path.html) without its final component, if there is one.

Returns [ None](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None) if the path terminates in a root or prefix.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-21)Examples

```
use camino::Utf8Path;
let path = Utf8Path::new("/foo/bar");
let parent = path.parent().unwrap();
assert_eq!(parent, Utf8Path::new("/foo"));
let grand_parent = parent.parent().unwrap();
assert_eq!(grand_parent, Utf8Path::new("/"));
assert_eq!(grand_parent.parent(), None);
```

#### pub fn [ancestors](https://docs.rs#method.ancestors)(&self) -> [Utf8Ancestors](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8Ancestors.html)<'_> [ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

The iterator will yield the [ Utf8Path](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8Path.html) that is returned if the

[method is used zero or more times. That means, the iterator will yield](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8Path.html#method.parent)

`parent``&self`, `&self.parent().unwrap()`,
`&self.parent().unwrap().parent().unwrap()` and so on. If the [method returns](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8Path.html#method.parent)

`parent`[, the iterator will do likewise. The iterator will always yield at least one value, namely](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None)

`None``&self`.[§](https://docs.rs#examples-22)Examples

```

let mut ancestors = Utf8Path::new("/foo/bar").ancestors();

assert_eq!(ancestors.next(), Some(Utf8Path::new("/foo")));

assert_eq!(ancestors.next(), None);
let mut ancestors = Utf8Path::new("../foo/bar").ancestors();

assert_eq!(ancestors.next(), Some(Utf8Path::new("../foo")));
assert_eq!(ancestors.next(), Some(Utf8Path::new("..")));
assert_eq!(ancestors.next(), Some(Utf8Path::new("")));
assert_eq!(ancestors.next(), None);
```

If the path is a normal file, this is the file name. If it’s the path of a directory, this is the directory name.

Returns [ None](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None) if the path terminates in

`..`.[§](https://docs.rs#examples-23)Examples

```

assert_eq!(Some("foo.txt"), Utf8Path::new("tmp/foo.txt").file_name());

```

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/camino/lib.rs.html#1300-1302)#### pub fn [components](https://docs.rs#method.components)(&self) -> [Utf8Components](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8Components.html)<'_> [ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/camino/lib.rs.html#1300-1302)

#### pub fn [components](https://docs.rs#method.components)(&self) -> [Utf8Components](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8Components.html)<'_> [ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

Produces an iterator over the [ Utf8Component](https://docs.rs/enum.Utf8Component.html)s of the path.

When parsing the path, there is a small amount of normalization:

-
Repeated separators are ignored, so `a/b`and`a//b`both have`a`and`b`as components.
-
Occurrences of `.`are normalized away, except if they are at the beginning of the path. For example,`a/./b`,`a/b/`,`a/b/.`and`a/b`all have`a`and`b`as components, but`./a/b`starts with an additional`CurDir`
-
A trailing slash is normalized away, `/a/b`and`/a/b/`are equivalent.

Note that no other normalization takes place; in particular, `a/c`
and `a/b/../c` are distinct, to account for the possibility that `b`
is a symbolic link (so its parent isn’t `a`).

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-35)Examples

```
use camino::{Utf8Component, Utf8Path};
let mut components = Utf8Path::new("/tmp/foo.txt").components();
assert_eq!(components.next(), Some(Utf8Component::RootDir));
assert_eq!(components.next(), Some(Utf8Component::Normal("tmp")));
assert_eq!(components.next(), Some(Utf8Component::Normal("foo.txt")));
assert_eq!(components.next(), None)
```
Produces an iterator over the path’s components viewed as [ str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html)
slices.

For more information about the particulars of how the path is separated
into components, see [ components](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8Path.html#method.components).

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-36)Examples

```
use camino::Utf8Path;
let mut it = Utf8Path::new("/tmp/foo.txt").iter();
assert_eq!(it.next(), Some(std::path::MAIN_SEPARATOR.to_string().as_str()));
assert_eq!(it.next(), Some("tmp"));
assert_eq!(it.next(), Some("foo.txt"));
assert_eq!(it.next(), None)
```
Queries the file system to get information about a file, directory, etc.

This function will traverse symbolic links to query information about the destination file.

This is an alias to [ fs::metadata](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/fs/fn.metadata.html).

```
use camino::Utf8Path;

```

Returns `true` if the path points at an existing entity.

Warning: this method may be error-prone, consider using [ try_exists()](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8Path.html#method.try_exists) instead!
It also has a risk of introducing time-of-check to time-of-use (TOCTOU) bugs.

This function will traverse symbolic links to query information about the
destination file. In case of broken symbolic links this will return `false`.

If you cannot access the directory containing the file, e.g., because of a
permission error, this will return `false`.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-45)Examples

```
use camino::Utf8Path;
assert!(!Utf8Path::new("does_not_exist.txt").exists());
```
[§](https://docs.rs#see-also)See Also

This is a convenience function that coerces errors to false. If you want to
check errors, call [ fs::metadata](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/fs/fn.metadata.html).

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/camino/lib.rs.html#1581-1587)#### pub fn [try_exists](https://docs.rs#method.try_exists)(&self) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/io/error/type.Result.html)<[bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/camino/lib.rs.html#1581-1587)

#### pub fn [try_exists](https://docs.rs#method.try_exists)(&self) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/io/error/type.Result.html)<[bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)>

Returns `Ok(true)` if the path points at an existing entity.

This function will traverse symbolic links to query information about the
destination file. In case of broken symbolic links this will return `Ok(false)`.

As opposed to the [ exists()](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8Path.html#method.exists) method, this one doesn’t silently ignore errors
unrelated to the path not existing. (E.g. it will return

[in case of permission denied on some of the parent directories.)](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html#variant.Err)

`Err`Note that while this avoids some pitfalls of the `exists()` method, it still can not
prevent time-of-check to time-of-use (TOCTOU) bugs. You should only use it in scenarios
where those bugs are not an issue.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-46)Examples

```
use camino::Utf8Path;
assert!(
    !Utf8Path::new("does_not_exist.txt")
        .try_exists()
        .expect("Can't check existence of file does_not_exist.txt")
);
assert!(Utf8Path::new("/root/secret_file.txt").try_exists().is_err());
```
Returns `true` if the path exists on disk and is pointing at a regular file.

This function will traverse symbolic links to query information about the
destination file. In case of broken symbolic links this will return `false`.

If you cannot access the directory containing the file, e.g., because of a
permission error, this will return `false`.
